chunks.title: Who is Ayush Yadav?
chunks.text: Ayush Yadav is an R&D Software Engineer II at Cadence Design Systems. He works on performance-critical systems, C++ performance engineering, distributed systems, agentic AI and developer tooling, with production wins on Apple, Google, Samsung and NVIDIA workloads.

chunks.title: What does Ayush focus on?
chunks.text: Ayush cares about end-to-end ownership: from low-level profiling and distributed-system design to polished, accessible product surfaces. His engineering principle is profile first — optimization without measurement is folklore.

chunks.title: MAESTRO — Multi-Agent Ticket Resolution
chunks.text: MAESTRO is a portable multi-agent platform Ayush built at Cadence: a conductor orchestrates 10 specialist AI agents across a 20-phase, human-gated workflow that carries an Xcelium engineering ticket from intake and root-cause analysis through fix, validation, review, regression and release. Measured across 22 Jiras, it cut ticket-resolution time by 45% and root-cause-analysis time by 55%, and it was selected for trade-secret protection.

chunks.title: ChipStack Xcelium AI agents for performance and memory
chunks.text: For Cadence ChipStack AI, Ayush built multi-agent Python workflows on the OpenAI Agents SDK that profile Xcelium simulations and apply and verify performance and memory fixes, achieving a 31.3% simulation speedup on a validated benchmark. A deterministic-first re-architecture cut end-to-end runtime from 148.3 s to 76.8 s (1.93x) and analysis from 71.1 s to 18.0 s (3.9x). He also built the shared agent framework with typed state, checkpoint and resume, structured outputs and fallback recovery, plus a YAML-driven LLM-as-judge regression framework.

chunks.title: Regression triage and Perforce replay tooling
chunks.text: Ayush built a ~16K-line Xcelium regression system using rule-based classification, TF-IDF clustering, historical learning and LLM review to automate triage, regolds, waivers and verification; it processed 2,120 failures across 79 runs, 73% of them in runs by other engineers. He also built cross-stream Perforce replay tooling that derives each changelist's source stream and selectively syncs only the paths it touches, automating multi-changelist backports across release branches.

chunks.title: Xcelium performance engineering
chunks.text: On Cadence's Xcelium logic simulator, Ayush did profiling-driven C++ optimization delivering +18 to 19% simulation throughput and +13 to 14% RTL transform runtime, validated on Apple, Google, Samsung and NVIDIA designs. He built a reusable Top-N profiling library presented at the Cadence India Conference.

chunks.title: AlgoLens — interactive DSA platform
chunks.text: AlgoLens is an open-source interactive algorithm visualizer supporting 60+ algorithms with deterministic step-through replay, in-browser FFmpeg-WASM video export, GenAI explanations and multi-modal search, held to WCAG 2.1 AA with Playwright, Sentry and CI quality gates.

chunks.title: PostureIQ — real-time ML posture analysis
chunks.text: PostureIQ is a 60 FPS computer-vision coaching system using MediaPipe/BlazePose pose estimation with Kalman filtering, confidence gating and rep-quality scoring around range of motion, tempo and symmetry, reaching over 95% accuracy.

chunks.title: Tezos Premier League
chunks.text: Tezos Premier League is a decentralized PvP gaming project and NFT marketplace on the Tezos blockchain, built with SmartPy, Taquito and IPFS. It was recognized with a $10,000 award for continued development.

chunks.title: Other projects
chunks.text: Other projects include Track Person App, a React Native movement-tracking app backed by MongoDB, and Smart Brain, a full-stack face-detection app integrating the Clarifai API with an Express and React surface.

chunks.title: What are Ayush's skills?
chunks.text: Ayush's core stack is C++ and Python for performance and systems work, plus TypeScript, React and Next.js for product surfaces. He works with LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector databases, profiling tools like Valgrind and AddressSanitizer, and developer tooling.

chunks.title: Competitive programming
chunks.text: Ayush stays sharp through competitive programming across LeetCode, Codeforces, CodeChef and HackerRank, keeping data-structures and algorithms fundamentals fast and reliable.

chunks.title: What is Ayush doing now?
chunks.text: Right now Ayush is doing R&D performance work on the Xcelium simulator, building multi-agent AI systems such as MAESTRO and the ChipStack Xcelium agents, and learning more about retrieval-augmented generation, distributed systems and vector databases at production scale.

chunks.title: System design
chunks.text: The portfolio includes interactive system-design whiteboards covering a URL shortener, a rate limiter and a job scheduler, with log analytics, a simulation regression dashboard and waveform compression sketched as coming soon.

chunks.title: How to contact Ayush
chunks.text: You can reach Ayush by email at aayush.sang@gmail.com, or connect on GitHub and LinkedIn. He is open to conversations about software engineering roles in C++ performance, distributed systems and AI tooling. Use the contact page to send a message.

chunks.title: Is Ayush open to roles?
chunks.text: Ayush is open to software engineering opportunities involving C++ performance, distributed systems and AI developer tooling. Enable Recruiter Mode on the site for a hiring-focused summary, or download his résumé and reach out via the contact page.
